properties.map: no map traced: outline constructed from the written description in Wikipedia, 'Great Fire of New York' (1835)
properties.note: Fire of 16-17 December 1835. Source text: 'The fire began ... in a five-story warehouse at 25 Merchant Street, now known as Beaver Street, at the intersection of Hanover Street and Wall Street ... The fire covered 17 city blocks and destroyed between 530 and 700 buildings. This part of the city is now known as Coenties Slip, an area between the East River and Maiden Lane in the north and William Street in the west.' Drawn from that: William St on the west, the East River (South St) on the east, Broad St / Coenties Slip on the south. North edge ESTIMATED at Wall St, not Maiden Lane: the area up to Maiden Lane holds about twice 17 blocks, the Merchants' Exchange on the south side of Wall St burned, and the usual account has the north side of Wall St saved; this was not checked against the 1836 maps of the burnt district. Colton's map of 1836 (manhattan_1836) already shades these blocks as built: rebuilding was immediate. Not a retreat: end the buildings inside it in 1835.
properties.method: ESTIMATED outline from a text, not from a map of the burnt district
